in_text_mentions: A 70-year-old Karen tribe woman had presented with non-follicular pustules on erythrodermic skin of her trunk and extremities since the age of 50. Nail psoriasis was also observed (Figure 1A–D,F). She had episodes approximately once a year. Diagnosis of GPP with erythroderma was made. No specific environmental or dietary triggers were noted. The rashes were well-controlled with rotational methotrexate and oral acitretin treatment. A skin biopsy from pustules on her abdomen showed subcorneal and spongiform pustules (Figure 1E).

The article title is disease-focused (Loss of Function TGFBR2 Variant as a Contributing Factor in Generalized Pustular Psoriasis and Adult-Onset Immunodeficiency) and the captioned manifestation (sterile non-follicular pustules) matches the provided GPP vocabulary, supporting attribution to generalized_pustular_psoriasis. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is an H&E histology image from a patient with GPP, showing subcorneal microabscesses (Munro microabscesses), a classic histopathologic feature of generalized pustular psoriasis. The caption notes the finding can also be seen in AGEP and the patient was initially suspected of having AGEP, so attribution is not fully specific, but the article title and clinical context support GPP. B: Panel B is a higher-magnification H&E view from the same pustular lesion biopsy, showing mild neutrophilic infiltration through the epidermis and mild dermal inflammation including occasional eosinophils. These features are compatible with GPP but the caption explicitly states they can be seen in both GPP and AGEP, lowering specificity; still, the panel belongs to a reported GPP case.
